options: Observe or use evidence, connect it to the concept, and explain the conclusion.

items.question: Explain food groups and give one everyday example.

options: Use major ideas independently in a new situation and explain the reasoning.
Finish the lesson without checking understanding.
items.explanation: Mastery requires independent transfer, not completion or copying.

items.question: What is the most important idea in 'Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body', and how would you teach it to a beginner?
items.answer: A defensible answer that identifies a foundational idea and teaches it accurately.

flashcards.back: Define food groups, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define balanced diet, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define nutrients, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore food groups
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on food groups. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where balanced diet is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach healthy choices to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
